# Canva Export & Sharing Guide

Best practices for exporting, saving, and sharing your Canva designs.

## Export Formats

### PDF (Recommended for Resumes)

**Best for**: Sharing with recruiters, applying to jobs, printing

**Steps**:
1. Click "Download" button (top right)
2. Select "PDF - Print"
3. Choose quality: "Standard" or "Premium"
4. Click "Download"

**Recommended settings**:
- Format: PDF
- Quality: Premium (for professional appearance)
- Page size: Letter (8.5" × 11") for US resumes

**File name**: `FirstName_LastName_Resume.pdf`

**Size**: Should be under 5MB

---

### PNG (For Digital Sharing)

**Best for**: Previewing online, social media, portfolios

**Steps**:
1. Click "Download" button
2. Select "PNG Image"
3. Choose quality: "Standard" or "Premium"
4. Click "Download"

**Recommended settings**:
- Quality: Premium
- Transparent background: Yes (optional)

**When to use**:
- Sharing on LinkedIn
- Digital portfolios
- Email signatures
- Social media

---

### JPG (Compressed Format)

**Best for**: Email, web, smaller file sizes

**Steps**:
1. Click "Download" button
2. Select "JPG Image"
3. Choose quality: "High" or "Premium"
4. Click "Download"

**File size**: Typically 100KB-300KB

**When to use**:
- Email attachments with file size limits
- Web uploads
- Compatibility with all devices

---

## Print Settings

### For Physical Printing

**Before printing**:
1. Export as PDF (Print quality)
2. Open PDF and verify:
   - All text is readable
   - Colors look correct
   - No elements are cut off
   - Page fits within margins

**Printer settings**:
- Paper size: Letter (8.5" × 11")
- Orientation: Portrait
- Quality: High or Best
- Paper type: Premium white or cream
- Color: Full color (or B&W if submitting to traditional firms)

**Pro tips**:
- Test print on regular paper first
- Print on quality resume paper for interviews
- Keep one high-quality PDF for digital submissions

---

## File Naming Conventions

### Professional File Names

✓ **Good examples**:
- `John_Smith_Resume.pdf`
- `Resume_John_Smith_2024.pdf`
- `SoftwareEngineer_JohnSmith.pdf`
- `John_Smith_Resume_Marketing.pdf` (for specific roles)

✗ **Avoid these**:
- `Resume.pdf` (too generic)
- `JSmith_Resume_Final_Final_FINAL.pdf` (unprofessional)
- `Untitled Document.pdf` (missing context)
- `John's resume.pdf` (apostrophes can cause issues)
- `Resume-HIRING_MANAGER_VERSION.pdf` (too informal)

### Version Control

If you have multiple versions:
- `John_Smith_Resume_Tech.pdf` (for tech roles)
- `John_Smith_Resume_Finance.pdf` (for finance roles)
- `John_Smith_Resume_2024.pdf` (dated version)

**Don't include**:
- Version numbers (v1, v2, etc.)
- Multiple dates
- Personal details in filename

---

## Quality Checklist Before Export

### Visual Check
- [ ] All text is black or your chosen color (not gray/faded)
- [ ] No text is cut off at page edges
- [ ] Colors look vibrant (not washed out)
- [ ] Images are sharp and clear
- [ ] No typos or formatting errors

### Technical Check
- [ ] Page is single-page (fits on one sheet)
- [ ] File size is under 5MB
- [ ] All fonts are embedded (not rendering as default)
- [ ] Links work correctly (if clickable PDF)
- [ ] PDF opens without errors

### Content Check
- [ ] Name is clearly visible at top
- [ ] Contact information is accurate and current
- [ ] Dates are correct and formatted consistently
- [ ] No outdated or irrelevant information
- [ ] Achievements include numbers/metrics

---

## Sharing Options

### Email

**Best practices**:
- Subject line: "Resume - [Your Name]" or "Resume - [Position] Role"
- Attach PDF as backup
- Also paste text version in email body (some systems screen emails for content)
- Use professional email address

**Example**:
```
Subject: Resume - John Smith - Software Engineer

Dear Hiring Manager,

Please find my resume attached. I'm excited about the opportunity 
and would love to discuss how my experience aligns with your needs.

Best regards,
John Smith
(555) 123-4567
john.smith@email.com
```

---

### LinkedIn

1. Go to your LinkedIn profile
2. Edit "Featured" section
3. Upload your resume as document
4. Make it public or private
5. Add description: "My current resume"

---

### Portfolio Website

1. Export as PNG or PDF
2. Upload to portfolio site
3. Make downloadable as PDF
4. Add link in "Download Resume" button
5. Update regularly

---

### ATS-Friendly Submission

**For online job applications**:

1. Export as PDF for downloading
2. Also have plain text version ready (copy-paste into form fields)
3. Don't use images within text areas
4. Use standard fonts and formatting
5. Avoid complex layouts

**Steps to create ATS text version**:
1. Copy all text from resume (no formatting)
2. Save in plain text file
3. Use for form fields that don't support PDF
4. Include keywords from job posting

---

## File Storage & Backup

### Recommended Setup

```
📁 Resume_Storage/
  📁 Current_Versions/
    └── John_Smith_Resume.pdf (Master)
  📁 Archive/
    ├── John_Smith_Resume_2023.pdf
    ├── John_Smith_Resume_2022.pdf
  📁 Variations/
    ├── John_Smith_Resume_Tech.pdf
    ├── John_Smith_Resume_Finance.pdf
  📁 Source_Files/
    └── John_Smith_Resume_Canva.link (or psd if exporting to other tools)
```

### Cloud Storage

- Google Drive: Easy sharing, version history
- Dropbox: Automatic syncing, link sharing
- OneDrive: Microsoft integration
- iCloud: Mac ecosystem (if applicable)

**Best practice**: Keep master in cloud, download locally for submissions

---

## Troubleshooting Export Issues

### Text Looks Blurry or Pixelated

**Solution**:
1. Use PDF export instead of PNG
2. Set quality to "Premium"
3. Verify font is web-safe (Montserrat, Lato, Open Sans)
4. Check that text size is at least 10pt

### Colors Look Different Than Preview

**Solution**:
1. Export as PDF (more accurate color representation)
2. Adjust color profile if needed
3. Test on different devices
4. Print to see actual color output

### File Size Too Large

**Solution**:
1. Use JPG instead of PNG
2. Select "Standard" quality instead of "Premium"
3. Reduce image resolution
4. Compress PDF after export (free tools: ilovepdf.com)

### Links Not Working in PDF

**Solution**:
1. Verify links are properly formatted
2. Re-export PDF
3. Test in PDF reader (not browser)
4. Use a tool to verify hyperlinks in PDF

### Missing Content When Printed

**Solution**:
1. Check printer margins (set to minimum)
2. Verify page size matches design (Letter 8.5×11")
3. Print preview before full print
4. Adjust design margins if needed

## Submission Tips

### Email Submission
- Use professional tone
- Introduce yourself briefly
- Include file name with your name
- Provide download link if using cloud storage

### Online Portal Submission
- Follow format requirements (PDF, DOC, etc.)
- Use file name with your name
- Don't add decorative elements
- Keep ATS compatibility in mind

### In-Person Interview
- Print on quality paper
- Bring 3-5 copies
- Single-sided printing
- Professional folder or portfolio

---

## Regular Updates

### When to Update Resume
- After new job or promotion
- After completing certification
- After significant project completion
- Quarterly review (add recent achievements)

### Annual Refresh
- Update contact information
- Add new skills and certifications
- Update employment dates
- Review and refine language
- Check for any typos

### Version Management
- Keep current version on desktop/mobile
- Archive old versions for reference
- Date archive files
- Delete outdated versions after 6 months
